name: redstone-torch-inverter
comment: Inverter (z = -4): a floor lever (69, meta 5) at x = -3, wire at x = -2, -1 into a stone block at x = 0, an active redstone torch (76) on the block's +x face (x = 1, oriented to meta 1 by BlockTorch.onBlockAdded) and wire x = 2, 3 behind it. The lever is switched on at t = 5 and off at t = 25 by set_block with meta 13 / 5 (BlockLever.onBlockRemoval reads the old metadata); the torch turns off two ticks after its block is powered and back on when it is not. Clock (z = 6): a stone block at x = 0, wire x = 2 at z = 6..9, then x = 1, 0 at z = 9 and x = 0 at z = 8, 7, running straight into the block's +z face; the torch on the block's +x face placed at t = 1 feeds the loop and turns itself off: BlockRedstoneTorch.torchUpdates fills, and the 8th turn-off within 100 ticks burns the torch out (random.fizz: two World.rand floats, 15 nextDouble smoke draws). At t = 130 a stone block above the torch makes it re-check (scheduleBlockUpdate from onNeighborBlockChange) after the history has expired.
